chunks: From him, from his father, from Fazalat ibn Ayyub, from Umar ibn Aban, from Jabir al-Ju'fi, who said:

I gathered myself in the presence of Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) and said, 'May I be your ransom! Sometimes I feel grief without a calamity befalling me or a matter descending upon me, to the extent that my family and my close friend recognize that in my face.' He (peace be upon him) said, 'Yes, O Jabir! Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, created the believers from the clay of Paradise and caused a spirit from His Spirit to flow among them. Therefore, the believer is a brother to the believer, like his father and mother. So if a spirit from those spirits in a city from the cities is struck by grief, this one is grieved because it is from them.'
ai.seo_question: Why do believers feel each other's grief and sorrow according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Kafi, Jabir al-Ju'fi recounts his experience of unexplained grief to Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him), who elucidates the metaphysical bond of believers through the concept of 'clay of Paradise' (Tinat al-Jinan). This spiritual kinship implies that believers share a single soul or essence, causing the emotional state of one to resonate with others, thereby reinforcing the practical implication of mutual empathy in Shia ethics. The narration highlights how this intrinsic connection transcends physical distance, making the grief of any believer a shared burden for the community.
